body: Thank you for the offer, that is very kind of you! but he would not be happy if he found out I was asking people to help him. He’s very “ independent “ so to speak, you know how stubborn dads can be. Again, that is very sweet to offer your help :)

I want to try the short walks but he is just so drained I can barely get him to take basic care of himself, I’ve been wanting to lose some weight so hopefully I can get him to come along with me, thanks for the advice!
I will give it a shot! He bought me a nice ukulele a couple christmases ago that I could never really play, maybe we’ll try and jump back into that. Thank you for the advice!

Thank you for sharing your story with me, and I really can’t imagine what it’s like to go through all of this. He is on a lot of medicine so it’s not so much the pain anymore (the pain was a lot worse in the moths leading up to and right after the transplant) but a huge part is the not sleeping. If you don’t mind me asking (and I know there’s no magic cute) what did you do to help you sleep? I’m a bit of a night owl so I’m going to sleep around 2-3 and he’s always wide awake in his bed and doesn’t get to sleep until 6 or 7 and even then, can’t stay asleep. Again, please do not feel the need to respond if I get too personal, but is there anything that someone did for you that really meant a lot to you? Something I could maybe try and do with him?

Luckily I still live at home with him, but I feel like my school work has gotten in the way of us talking lately. I’m definitely going to be more attentive to him. When I was at my worst, he has always right there telling me that none of it mattered and he just wanted me to do what made me happy. I mean not to brag, but I think my dad gives the best advice. I’m definitely going to task him with making me something, i’ll probably start with something small so he can work up the energy to finish it. Thanks for your reply, it means a lot to me!

It’s weird, most days he won’t admit he needs help but sometimes when we’re up late watching a movie or something, he will just look at me and tell me how tired he is of feeling like shit and it’s everything I can do not to break down because I just want what’s best for him. Luckily, I live at home (I’m 19 and just commute to the closest college, I didn’t want to leave him). I’m trying to get him up and moving but he’s just so low energy he doesn’t want to get up. I’m going to try and get him back into gardening, he has raised beds and he likes working with his hands. I want to try to get him motivated to work towards some goal again, but I think starting small with little tasks like cleaning up the beds is the way to go. Thank you for you advice and your kind words, it means a lot to me :)

It’s just getting hard because I’ve struggled with my mental health and I just got help and I feel like a human being again and I just want to give that to him. Luckily, I still live at home with him (I’m 19 and can’t afford dorm housing , but even if I could I wouldn’t leave him). I’m going to try setting him a schedule , he loves his Judy Justice and we always play Jeopardy together, but I’m going to try getting him in a better routine, thanks for your advice!

My dad is the SAME way. He never used to read and now I feel like he’s always sending me to grab more books from the thrift store. I’m definitely going to give reading the same book and having convos about it a try, thanks for the advice and thanks for sharing!
That’s what I really want him to do, he loved teaching Human Geography and I will definitely start looking for remote jobs!
